question: In Arctic-Text2SQL-R1, what reward does a query get if it is syntactically valid and executes but returns a different result from the gold result?
answer: Không đủ bằng chứng để trả lời.

events.query: Arctic-Text2SQL-R1 reward syntactically valid query executes different result than gold result reward scoring

results.text: The reward is deliberately simple: 1 if the query’s execution result matches the gold result, 0.1 if the query is syntactically valid and executes but returns a different result, and 0 otherwise. Combined with carefully filtered training data, strong supervised initialization (from OmniSQL checkpoints), and online training, this simple reward lets the model handle SQL aliasing and semantically equivalent variants naturally, and even the 7B variant matches earlier 70B-class systems. Databricks RLVR-32B: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards.Databricks Mosaic Research advanced Text-to-SQL reasoning through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) [1, 16]. Unlike approaches that depend on proxy or learned reward models, RLVR exploits rewards derived directly from the correctness of SQL execution, simplifying the training pipeline and grounding supervision in the task itself.

Values are taken as reported and mix BIRD development and test splits, so they indicate broad trends rather than a controlled comparison. In the first stage, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct is fine-tuned onSynSQL-200K, a balanced 200,000-example subset of the 2.5M-example synthetic SynSQL-2.5M corpus that covers a range of query complexities; this “cold start” instills basic schema linking, SQL syntax, and the reasoning-trace format. In the second stage, GRPO is applied toSynSQL-Complex-5K, a curated set of 5,000 challenging NL–SQL pairs requiring multi-table joins and nested subqueries. The composite reward comprises (1) aformat rewardthat enforces structured reasoning traces (delimited by <think> and <answer> tags), (2) anexecution rewardthat penalizes non-executable SQL, (3) aresult reward based on execution correctness, and (4) alength rewardthat balances reasoning detail against verbosity. With only 7B parameters, SQL-R1 reports 88.6% execution accuracy on Spider and 66.6% on the BIRD development set, demonstrating strong data efficiency while keeping its reasoning interpretable.

results.text: Starting from Qwen2.5-32B-Coder-Instruct [ 65], the team first warm-started the model with Test-time Adaptive Optimization (TAO), an offline RL method, and then applied online RLVR training. Using no data beyond the BIRD training set and no proprietary models, the resulting model reached 73.56% execution accuracy on the BIRD test set in the singlemodel, single-generation setting (surpassing the previous best single-model result of 71.83%) and 75.68% with self-consistency, highlighting the effectiveness of simple verifiable rewards for enterprise-grade Text-to-SQL. ExCoT: Execution-Guided Chain-of-Thought (Snowflake, March 2025).ExCoT [ 95] combines chain-of-thought reasoning withDirect Preference Optimization (DPO)[ 66] to improve both interpretability and execution accuracy. The 32B and 70B variants of Arctic-ExCoT achieve 68.19% and 68.53% execution accuracy, respectively, on the BIRD test set. ExCoT uses a two-phase training pipeline.

Holding the RLVR algorithm fixed, training on BIRD-Verified instead of the original training set improves single-generation accuracy by 8.2–13.9 absolute points, showing that data quality alone accounts for a substantial share of the apparent gap. At inference time, ReViSQL samples multiple candidates from the RLVR-trained policy and uses thepre-RLVR base modelas an independent referee for execution-based reconciliation: candidates whose interpretation drifts from the user’s stated intent are filtered out before a majority vote selects the final query. This mitigates the diversity collapse and over-confident “intent fixing” commonly observed after on-policy RL fine-tuning. The framework is released at two scales:ReViSQL-235B-A22B, which reaches human-level performance, andReViSQL30B-A3B, a cost-efficient Mixture-of-Experts variant that matches the prior open-source state of the art at roughly 7.5× lower per-query inference cost.

answer: Không đủ bằng chứng để trả lời.

events.query: MAC-SQL Selector agent role what does Selector do

results.text: MAC-SQL.MAC-SQL [ 80] proposes a multi-agent collaborative pipeline comprising three agents: aSelector, aDecomposer, and aRefiner. The Selector filters the schema to retain only relevant tables and columns, reducing token overhead; the Decomposer applies chain-of-thought reasoning to break complex questions into sub-problems; and the Refiner executes candidate queries, collects errors or empty results, and iteratively fixes the outputs using this feedback. The framework is instantiated with GPT-4 for maximum accuracy and with SQL-Llama (Section 5.3) for open-source deployment. MAC-SQL set a new state of the art on BIRD at the time of publication (59.59% execution accuracy on the test set) and is competitive on Spider; its ablations show that each agent contributes to performance, confirming the value of multi-agent collaboration and error recovery. 24

5.4 Agentic Methods Agent-based approaches have emerged as a powerful paradigm for improving semantic alignment, modular interpretability, and execution correctness in complex query generation. By coordinating multiple LLM-driven agents and external tools, these systems decompose, validate, and refine SQL queries with higher accuracy and robustness than monolithic architectures. This section surveys a range of recent agentic frameworks that exemplify the shift toward collaborative, multi-step processing. ReFoRCE.ReFoRCE [ 17] addresses the practical failure modes of large-scale, cross-domain Textto-SQL by combining schema compression, execution-guided self-refinement, and selective column exploration in a single agentic pipeline. The system first reduces prompt bloat by grouping similarly named tables by pattern and retaining representative table DDLs and sample rows, and then runs a lightweight LLM-driven schema linker to select task-relevant tables and columns.

results.text: The approach attains state-of-the-art execution accuracy on the Spider development set (91.6%) and strong robustness on Spider-Realistic (90.2%) and Spider-Syn (82.0%), with a very high rate of valid SQL; ablations show that removing either the query-planning stage or the taxonomy-guided correction loop causes substantial accuracy drops. The authors also characterize practical trade-offs: multi-agent planning and iterative correction substantially increase token and latency costs, and they suggest hybrid deployments (stronger models for planning, cheaper models for generation) to balance cost and performance. SQL-of-Thought is therefore particularly attractive when correctness and auditability are priorities, albeit at higher compute and engineering cost. CHASE-SQL: multi-path reasoning and candidate selection.Traditional Text-to-SQL systems often rely on single-shot generation, which limits their robustness on complex queries.

Key characteristics that distinguish Spider 2.0 from earlier benchmarks include: – Execution-centric evaluation.Scoring is based on whether the produced results are correct when executed against the target databases, which allows single-shot parsers, prompt-based LLMs, and multi-stage agentic systems to be compared on a common footing rather than by surface-form matching. – Multi-stage workflows.Many tasks require multi-step interaction: inspecting the schema, issuing partial queries, examining intermediate results, and performing repair or validation steps. This exposes failure modes that single-shot benchmarks cannot capture. 6

• Spider 2.0[ 46]: a next-generation evaluation framework of 632 real-world enterprise workflow problems that extends the canonical Spider task toend-to-end problem solvingover relational databases. Tasks are drawn from enterprise-scale databases hosted on cloud and local systems (e.g., BigQuery, Snowflake, SQLite), frequently involve schemas with more than a thousand columns, and may require multiple SQL dialects, project-level codebases, and lengthy queries. Spider 2.0 is designed to reflect realistic analytical workflows: it evaluates not only single-shot NL→SQL parsers but also multi-stage pipelines and autonomous agents that inspect schemas, issue exploratory queries, validate execution, and repair errors. Two derived settings,Spider 2.0-Lite andSpider 2.0-Snow, isolate the pure Text-to-SQL component.

• Execution accuracy (EX)can overestimate performance when incorrect queries coincidentally return the correct result, and it requires full access to the underlying database, which is not always feasible. • Valid efficiency score (VES)is sensitive to execution latency and system-specific factors, limiting its reliability across environments. • AST-based similarity metrics (e.g., TSED)incur higher computational overhead and have seen limited adoption because of their implementation complexity. results.text: The task is formulated as a partially observable Markov decision process whose hidden state is the full schema and whose observations are limited to what the agent’s metadata-inspection tools return. On top of this formulation, TRUST-SQL imposes afour-phase interaction protocol:Explore(schema-discovery tool calls such as table listing, column inspection, and row sampling),Propose(explicit commitment to a verified subset of tables, columns, and join paths),Generate(SQL conditioned on the proposed schema), andConfirm(execution and validation of the result). The Propose phase acts as amandatory cognitive checkpoint: in a pilot study, schema hallucinations (references to tables or columns that do not exist) account for 26.4% of failures in a vanilla execution-correction baseline, 14.2% when execution feedback alone is added, and only 2.8% once the Propose checkpoint is introduced (a 9.4-fold reduction).

Conceptually, SQL-Trail bridges the RL paradigm of this section and the agentic paradigm of Section 5.4: the iteration loops hand-engineered into systems such as MAC-SQL and CHASE-SQL can instead belearnedas part of an RL-trained policy. TRUST-SQL: tool-integrated multi-turn RL over unknown schemas (March 2026).TRUST-SQL [38] extends the multi-turn RL paradigm of SQL-Trail to a more realistic deployment setting that exposes a hidden assumption shared by essentially every method in this survey: theFull Schema Assumption, whereby the complete database schema is injected into the model’s context alongside the question. Real enterprise databases contain hundreds to thousands of tables with voluminous and noisy metadata, making upfront schema injection infeasible. TRUST-SQL therefore studies theUnknown Schemascenario, in which the agent starts with no schema knowledge and must actively discover, inspect, and verify the relevant subset before generating any SQL.

Holding the protocol, backbone, and training data constant, Dual-Track GRPO yields a 9.9% relative improvement over standard GRPO. Training uses Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B backbones, with a supervised cold-start phase followed by Dual-Track GRPO with PPO-style clipped updates. Across five Text-to-SQL benchmarks, TRUSTSQL delivers average absolute execution-accuracy improvements of30.6points for the 4B variant and 16.6points for the 8B variant over their respective base models; the larger gain for the smaller model suggests that structured agentic protocols benefit compact models disproportionately. Most importantly for deployment, TRUST-SQL operates entirelywithout a preloaded schemayet consistently matches or surpasses strong baselines that rely on full schema injection. 20

results.text: Cortex Analyst (Snowflake).Cortex Analyst [ 74] is Snowflake’s enterprise-grade agentic framework for Text-to-SQL, designed to let non-technical users interact with structured data. At its core is a semantic model encoded in YAML that captures domain-specific table and column metadata, relationships, and synonyms. An orchestrator coordinates several specialized components: a relationships agent infers join paths, a semantic-model editor updates metadata using execution traces, a custom-instruction agent injects domain-specific behavior, and an evaluator agent performs multi-step validation. SQL generation is guided by Claude 3.5 Sonnet and refined through an execution-feedback loop. Snowflake reports roughly 90% execution accuracy on real-world business-intelligence datasets, an improvement of about 20–30% over LLM-only approaches.

5.4 Agentic Methods Agent-based approaches have emerged as a powerful paradigm for improving semantic alignment, modular interpretability, and execution correctness in complex query generation. By coordinating multiple LLM-driven agents and external tools, these systems decompose, validate, and refine SQL queries with higher accuracy and robustness than monolithic architectures. This section surveys a range of recent agentic frameworks that exemplify the shift toward collaborative, multi-step processing. ReFoRCE.ReFoRCE [ 17] addresses the practical failure modes of large-scale, cross-domain Textto-SQL by combining schema compression, execution-guided self-refinement, and selective column exploration in a single agentic pipeline. The system first reduces prompt bloat by grouping similarly named tables by pattern and retaining representative table DDLs and sample rows, and then runs a lightweight LLM-driven schema linker to select task-relevant tables and columns.

small language models (SLMs, each under 8B parameters): aBase Action Model(BAM) that converts an initial SQL candidate into an explicitaction trajectory(a stepwise reasoning trace), aSchema Augmentation Model(SAM) that refines schema bindings and table/column alignments within the trajectory, and aLogic Optimization Model(LOM) that corrects semantic and logical defects before the final SQL is reconstructed. The components are trained with ahierarchical self-evolutionscheme in which each SLM is progressively specialized with compact, task-specific supervision, so as to localize errors precisely and improve repair accuracy with minimal data. By operating on intermediate action trajectories rather than raw SQL text, SHARE achieves fine-grained error localization and substantially reduces end-to-end compute compared with monolithic LLM recursion.

Additional structure-oriented metrics used in practice include: • Component Matching (CM).Used in the Spider benchmark, CM breaks each SQL query into its main components, including SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY , ORDER BY , and keywords. For each component, it computes an F1 score between the predicted and ground-truth sets of sub-components while ignoring order. This enables fine-grained analysis of which parts of a query are generated correctly. • Exact Set Match (EM without values).Also used in Spider, this metric evaluates structural equivalence by treating the tables, columns, and operators within each clause as unordered sets and ignoring constant values. By focusing on structure rather than surface form, it credits semantically equivalent rewrites even when literal values differ. 13

It fully fine-tunes CodeLlama-Instruct models (7B to 34B parameters) on SKGInstruct, an instruction-tuning dataset of roughly 1.1M examples spanning 18 tasks over tables, databases, and knowledge graphs, including Text-to-SQL datasets such as Spider and CoSQL. StructLM outperforms task-specific models on the majority of the evaluated datasets, and the authors observe that scaling from 7B to 34B brings only marginal gains, suggesting that structure-aware training data matters more than model size for this family of tasks. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning.Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) updates only a small subset of weights (e.g., adapter modules, low-rank matrices [ 18, 34], or output heads) while freezing the majority of pretrained parameters. This reduces GPU memory use and training time while preserving most of the original model’s linguistic generalization, which makes it attractive for domain-specific and privacy-sensitive deployments.

Execution Accuracy (EX) and Valid Efficiency Score (VES) require database access but capture semantic correctness, whereas structure-aware metrics such as SQAM and TSED provide partial credit and syntactic fidelity without requiring query execution, making them suitable for privacy-restricted or compliance-sensitive deployment settings. No single metric covers all properties, reinforcing the need for multi-metric evaluation protocols. 4.8 Challenges in Evaluation Although these metrics have helped standardize evaluation, each has limitations: • Exact match (EM)does not account for the syntactic flexibility of SQL and therefore penalizes queries that are logically correct but written in an alternative form.

Conversational quality metrics.For multi-turn benchmarks such as SParC and CoSQL, evaluation typically includes the following measures: • Turn-level execution accuracy:the proportion of individual dialogue turns for which the generated SQL executes correctly, taking into account the conversational context carried over from previous turns. • Dialogue success rate:the proportion of complete dialogues in which all turns are answered correctly, capturing the system’s ability to preserve context and behave coherently throughout the interaction. • Response fluency (BLEU):for system-generated natural language responses such as clarification questions or confirmations, BLEU or related n-gram overlap metrics assess fluency and similarity to reference utterances. Summary.Evaluation in Text-to-SQL has matured significantly, with EM and EX forming the core of most benchmarks. VES and TSA offer important extensions for assessing efficiency and generalization under more stringent testing.
